screening.reason: Inclusion 2,3: resting-state fMRI group-difference analysis (ASD vs HC) on ABIDE I, used as one of two multi-site test cases for a site-effect mitigation method (site-wise de-meaning), with an ASD-vs-control effect-size evaluation (not a software-only benchmark, since it quantifies preservation of a known autism-vs-control FC finding).

evidence_spans.text: We present a site-wise de-meaning (SWD) strategy in multi-site FC analysis and compare its performance with two common site-effect mitigation methods, i.e., generalized linear model (GLM) and Combining Batches (ComBat) Harmonization.
evidence_spans.claim: Main method: site-wise de-meaning (SWD) compared against GLM and ComBat for multi-site FC harmonisation.

evidence_spans.text: Resting-state fMRI data from 850 subjects in ABIDE I with an ASD DSM-IV-TR diagnosis (n = 355) and the corresponding HCs (n = 495) from the same sites were used in this study
evidence_spans.claim: Analysed ABIDE I cohort: 355 ASD, 495 HC (850 total).

evidence_spans.text:
The resting-state fMRI data was preprocessed using the
Connectome Computation System pipeline (Zuo et al., 2013).

The resting state fMRI data was then parcellated into
200 regions of interest (ROIs) using a spatially constrained
spectral clustering algorithm based on functional parcellations by
Cameron Craddock (Craddock et al., 2012).

The most common resting state
fMRI ﬁnding regarding ASD FC was anterior-posterior DMN
hypoconnectivity
evidence_spans.claim: Literature-anchored ASD finding used as the test feature: anterior-posterior default mode network hypoconnectivity (MPFC-PCC/precuneus).

evidence_spans.text: For the ABIDE dataset, SWD improved the effect size between autistic and control subjects by 2.9–5.3%, while GLM and ComBat decreased the effect size by up to 11.4%.
evidence_spans.claim: Main result: SWD improves ASD-vs-control effect size by 2.9-5.3%, while GLM/ComBat reduce it by up to 11.4%.

evidence_spans.text: Autism data is publicly available from ABIDE (http://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.org/indi/abide/)
evidence_spans.claim: Data availability: ABIDE data publicly available at the stated URL.

assessments.support: "Resting-state fMRI data from 850 subjects in ABIDE I with an ASD DSM-IV-TR diagnosis (n = 355) and the corresponding HCs (n = 495) from the same sites were used in this study".
Demographic information including site, sample size, sex and age is given in a table, per the text referencing Table 1/Table 4 for ABIDE sites.

"The resting-state fMRI data was preprocessed using the
Connectome Computation System pipeline (Zuo et al., 2013)." with full preprocessing steps listed (slice-timing, motion correction, nuisance regression, bandpass filtering).
"Resting-state fMRI data from 850 subjects in ABIDE I with an ASD DSM-IV-TR diagnosis (n = 355)" — diagnosis source (DSM-IV-TR) explicitly stated.

Age and sex are regressed out ("linear regression was used to regress out age
and sex covariates"); site is the central confounder the entire paper is designed to address.
Site effects handled via three compared methods (GLM, ComBat, and the proposed site-wise de-meaning), directly testing which best preserves the diagnostic group effect.
Pearson correlation FC, Fisher z-transformed, with Hedge's g effect size relative to a literature-anchored finding (anterior-posterior DMN hypoconnectivity).

Effect sizes (Hedge's g) are reported for specific literature-selected ROI pairs rather than a whole-brain corrected statistical test, so multiple-comparison correction is not directly applicable/reported for this effect-size preservation analysis.

risk_of_bias.summary: Cohort, diagnosis source, pipeline and atlas are all explicitly reported, and the paper's central contribution is a rigorous, quantitative comparison of site-effect handling methods (GLM, ComBat, SWD) on preserving a known ASD-vs-control connectivity effect; the main caveat is that the evaluation targets specific literature-anchored ROI pairs rather than a whole-brain multiple-comparison-corrected analysis.

charting.feature_extraction_tools: Connectome Computation System (CCS) pipeline (slice-timing correction, motion correction, skull stripping, global mean intensity normalization, nuisance regression, 0.01-0.1Hz bandpass filtering)
charting.specific_features: Seed/ROI-to-ROI resting-state functional connectivity (Pearson correlation, Fisher z-transformed), Craddock 200 (CC200) atlas (200 ROIs)
charting.performance_metrics: Hedge's g effect size (patients vs. controls) compared across original data, GLM, ComBat, and the proposed site-wise de-meaning (SWD) method
charting.key_performance_results: SWD improved the ASD-vs-control effect size by 2.9-5.3% relative to the original data; GLM and ComBat decreased the effect size by up to 11.4% and 7.5%/5.1% respectively for the primary feature
charting.features_associated_disorder: Anterior-posterior default mode network connectivity: MPFC-PCC/precuneus and MPFC-MTG
charting.feature_change_direction: Hypoconnectivity in ASD (reduced MPFC-PCC/precuneus and MPFC-MTG connectivity), consistent with the literature-reported hypoconnectivity hypothesis of ASD
charting.dataset_openly_available: Yes — ABIDE data publicly available at http://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.org/indi/abide/; no separate analysis code repository mentioned

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational) / methods-comparison study; ABIDE I, 850 subjects (355 ASD, 495 HC) from multiple sites
narrative_row.methods: CCS-preprocessed resting-state functional connectivity (CC200 atlas, Fisher z-transformed), compared across three site-effect mitigation strategies (GLM, ComBat, and the proposed site-wise de-meaning) using Hedge's g effect size on a literature-anchored ASD finding (anterior-posterior DMN hypoconnectivity)
narrative_row.outcomes: Site-wise de-meaning (SWD) improved ASD-vs-control effect size by 2.9-5.3% relative to uncorrected data, while GLM and ComBat reduced it by up to 11.4% and 7.5% respectively, indicating SWD better preserves disorder-related connectivity signal under multi-site harmonisation
narrative_row.key_limitations: Evaluation restricted to specific literature-selected ROI pairs rather than a whole-brain corrected analysis; no code repository identified beyond the public ABIDE data link
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Directly addresses RQ on site handling (CL6) with a quantitative comparison of three site-effect mitigation strategies applied to ABIDE I resting-state connectivity.

kg_link.cohort_description: 850 subjects with resting-state fMRI from ABIDE I: 355 ASD (DSM-IV-TR diagnosis) and 495 HC from the same sites
kg_link.finding: Site-wise de-meaning (SWD) improved the ASD-vs-control functional connectivity effect size (Hedge's g) by 2.9-5.3% relative to uncorrected data, better preserving anterior-posterior DMN hypoconnectivity than GLM or ComBat harmonisation (which decreased effect size by up to 11.4%)
evidence_quotes: Resting-state fMRI data from 850 subjects in ABIDE I with an ASD DSM-IV-TR diagnosis (n = 355) and the corresponding HCs (n = 495) from the same sites were used in this study
For the ABIDE dataset, SWD improved the effect size between autistic and control subjects by 2.9–5.3%, while GLM and ComBat decreased the effect size by up to 11.4%.
Autism data is publicly available from ABIDE (http://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.org/indi/abide/)
